description: Bind a human-readable name to a target you want to remember by identity instead of id. The naming is YOURS — 'the toilet', 'the shrub-trap', 'Kelly's spot', 'joao's place'. Once named, use it in go-to with --my_name, or in visit-lot with --my_name (for lot bindings). Exactly one target kind per call: target_object_id (a VMEntity), target_sim_id (a Sim persist id), location (tile x,y,level — for naming a spot, not an object), or lot_location (a lot location code — for naming a lot you can visit-lot to). Names are case-insensitive on lookup; the original case is preserved for display. Re-naming overwrites. Storage is sidecar-local and session-scoped (lost on bot restart — identity continuation across sessions is -38a). This verb removes the need to carry ObjectIDs or lot location codes in your working memory; your private vocabulary of the world is what lets you talk about it like a place instead of a data structure.

args.name: as
args.description: The name you are giving this target. Free-form. Case-insensitive on lookup.

args.name: target_object_id
args.description: ObjectID of the thing you're naming (e.g. a toilet, a sofa, a door).

args.name: target_sim_id
args.description: Persist id of the Sim you're naming.

args.name: location
args.description: {"x": tile_x, "y": tile_y, "level": 1}. Tile units. Use for naming a spot with no object there ('the shrub-trap', 'the corner I got stuck').

args.name: lot_location
args.description: Lot location code ('0x00F8F100' hex or decimal uint32). Use for naming a lot so you can visit-lot --my_name later. The value is the same packed location code from perception.lot.lot_id or find-avatar's lot_location field.

args.name: note
args.description: Optional free-form note stored with the name. Surfaces in list-names.

call_signatures: cf $CF name --as "the toilet" --target_object_id 322                               # name an object
cf $CF name --as Kelly --target_sim_id 4                                            # name a Sim
cf $CF name --as "the shrub-trap" --location '{"x":2,"y":6,"level":1}'           # name a spot
cf $CF name --as "joao's place" --lot_location 0x00F8F100                          # name a lot (use with visit-lot --my_name)
common_mistakes: Passing both --target_object_id and --location: only one target kind per name.
Using tile-scale coords for location in 1/16-tile units (wire units). Location is TILE units — the coords you see in perception.avatar.position.
Passing lot_id (DB integer) as lot_location — these are different. Use the packed location code (same value as perception.lot.lot_id or find-avatar's lot_location field).
Relying on names across sessions today. Storage is session-scoped; persistent names across reboots await -38a.
perception_hints: Current position for location-type names: perception.avatar.position (tile units)
See what you've already named: list-names
refuse_conditions: no target selector → ok:false with 'one of target_object_id, target_sim_id, or location is required'
more than one target selector → ok:false
location missing x or y → ok:false
